We observe that the pseudo-distance $d_T$ is not a distance. For example, we can consider the two Abelian groups $\bigoplus_{i=1}^\infty \mathbb{Z}$ (obtained by adding infinite copies of the integer numbers) and  $\mathbb{Z}_2\oplus\bigoplus_{i=1}^\infty \mathbb{Z}$. We can find two topological spaces $X$, $Y$ such that their homology groups in degree $1$ are these two groups, respectively. If we take the two filtering functions $\varphi:X\to\mathbb{R}$, $\psi:Y\to\mathbb{R}$ with $\varphi\equiv\psi\equiv 0$, we have that $H^{(X,\varphi)}_k(u,v)=\bigoplus_{i=1}^\infty \mathbb{Z}$ and $H^{(Y,\psi)}_k(u,v)= \mathbb{Z}_2\oplus\bigoplus_{i=1}^\infty \mathbb{Z}$ for any $(u,v)\in \Delta^+$ with $u\ge 0$. Obviously, if $(u,v)\in \Delta^+$ with $u< 0$ we get that both $H^{(X,\varphi)}_k(u,v)$ and $H^{(Y,\psi)}_k(u,v)$ are the trivial group. In any case, it is easy to find a surjective homomorphism from $ H^{(X,\varphi)}_k(u,v)$ onto $ H^{(Y,\psi)}_k(u,v)$ and a surjective homomorphism from $H^{(Y,\psi)}_k(u,v)$ onto $ H^{(X,\varphi)}_k(u,v)$, so that $d_T\left( H^{(X,\varphi)}_k, H^{(Y,\psi)}_k\right)=0$. However, the groups $H^{(X,\varphi)}_k(u,v), H^{(Y,\psi)}_k(u,v)$ are not isomorphic, for $(u,v)\in \Delta^+$ with $u\ge 0$.
